font-default.question: How do I use this font generator?
font-default.answer: Simply type or paste your text in the input box above. The styled text will appear instantly below. Click the Copy button to copy it to your clipboard, then paste it wherever you want — social media, messages, documents, etc.

font-default.question: Will this font work on Instagram/Twitter/Discord?
font-default.answer: Yes! Unicode text works on virtually all platforms including Instagram, Twitter/X, Discord, Facebook, WhatsApp, TikTok, and more. The styled characters are real Unicode code points, not formatting — so they work in any text field.

font-default.question: Why do some characters not change?
font-default.answer: Unicode doesn't have styled versions of all characters. Punctuation, spaces, and some special characters will remain unchanged. Some font styles only support uppercase or lowercase letters.

font-default.question: Is this free to use?
font-default.answer: Yes, Fontify is completely free with no limits. You can generate as much styled text as you want without signing up or paying anything.

symbols-default.question: How do I copy a symbol?
symbols-default.answer: Simply click on any symbol in the grid above. It will be automatically copied to your clipboard. You'll see a confirmation message when it's copied successfully.

symbols-default.question: Where can I use these symbols?
symbols-default.answer: These Unicode symbols work everywhere that supports text input — social media posts, messages, emails, documents, website content, and more. They're real characters, not images.

symbols-default.question: Why doesn't a symbol display correctly?
symbols-default.answer: Some symbols require modern font support. If a symbol appears as a box or question mark, your device or browser may not have a font that includes that character. Try updating your system or using a different device.

tools-default.question: How does this text tool work?
tools-default.answer: Type or paste your text in the input area above. The tool will automatically transform it using Unicode characters or special formatting techniques. Click Copy to copy the result to your clipboard.

tools-default.question: Will the transformed text work everywhere?
tools-default.answer: Most tools use Unicode characters which work on all platforms. Some tools (like spoiler text) use platform-specific formatting that only works on certain apps like Discord.

tools-default.question: Is my text stored anywhere?
tools-default.answer: No. All transformations happen in your browser. Your text is never sent to any server or stored anywhere. Everything is processed locally on your device.

use-case-default.question: Are these fonts safe to use on social media?
use-case-default.answer: Yes! Unicode fonts are just regular text characters and don't violate any platform's terms of service. They work like normal text but look different because they use alternate Unicode character sets.

use-case-default.question: Will fancy fonts affect my reach or engagement?
use-case-default.answer: Using fancy fonts sparingly can increase engagement by making your posts stand out. However, excessive use may reduce readability. It's best to use styled text for headers, bios, or key words rather than entire paragraphs.

use-case-default.question: Do these fonts work on all devices?
use-case-default.answer: Most Unicode fonts display correctly on modern smartphones, tablets, and computers. Very old devices or systems with limited font support may not render all characters correctly.

zalgo.question: What is Zalgo text?
zalgo.answer: Zalgo text (also called glitch text or corrupted text) uses Unicode combining diacritical marks stacked on top of and below regular characters. This creates a chaotic, glitchy appearance that looks like the text is being corrupted or consumed by darkness.

zalgo.question: Why is it called Zalgo?
zalgo.answer: The name comes from a creepypasta internet meme about 'Zalgo' — a fictional eldritch entity. The corrupted text style became associated with horror and cosmic dread themes online.

zalgo.question: Can Zalgo text crash apps?
zalgo.answer: Very intense Zalgo text (with many combining marks) can sometimes cause rendering issues in apps that don't handle complex Unicode well. Use the intensity options to control how extreme the effect is.

strikethrough.question: How does Unicode strikethrough work?
strikethrough.answer: Unicode strikethrough uses the Combining Long Stroke Overlay character (U+0336) placed after each character. This tells the rendering system to draw a line through the preceding character, creating a strikethrough effect without platform-specific formatting.

strikethrough.question: Is this different from regular strikethrough?
strikethrough.answer: Yes. Regular strikethrough (like in Word or HTML) uses text formatting that may not survive when copied to other apps. Unicode strikethrough uses combining characters that are part of the text itself, so it works when pasted anywhere.

bold.question: How does Unicode bold text work?
bold.answer: Unicode bold uses Mathematical Sans-Serif Bold characters (U+1D5D4 onwards). These are separate code points that look like bold versions of regular letters. They're actual characters in Unicode, not formatting — so they display as bold everywhere.

bold.question: Can I use bold text in Instagram bios?
bold.answer: Yes! Unicode bold text works perfectly in Instagram bios, captions, and comments. Simply generate your bold text here, copy it, and paste it directly into Instagram.

bold.question: Why doesn't bold work for numbers in some styles?
bold.answer: Some Unicode font styles only include letters (A-Z, a-z) and not digits. When a style doesn't have bold number variants, the regular numbers will appear unchanged.

cursive.question: What makes cursive Unicode text special?
cursive.answer: Cursive Unicode uses Mathematical Script characters that look like flowing handwritten text. Unlike using a cursive font (which only works where that font is installed), Unicode cursive text carries its styling with it everywhere you paste it.

cursive.question: Why do some cursive letters look different from others?
cursive.answer: A few cursive characters in Unicode have alternative forms or are taken from different blocks. This is because the mathematical script characters weren't originally designed as a consistent 'font' — they were meant for mathematical notation.
